faqHeading.title: Frequently asked questions.
faqHeading.intro: Practical answers for choosing a level range, matching liquid and vessel conditions, installing the probe and connecting readings to your operating workflow.

faqs.question: What level range should I choose for my tank, well or sump?
paragraphs: Start with the highest level you need to measure, the probe reference point and the level tolerance required by your operation. The published H Series family covers 0–200 m with customization available. Select the actual full-scale range for the installation rather than using the widest range automatically. A tank drawing, well depth or sump section helps Hitelecom review the range, cable length and mounting together.

faqs.question: How does full-scale accuracy relate to my tank depth?
paragraphs: The published accuracy is ±0.5% FS, meaning a percentage of the selected full scale. As a calculation example, a 10 m full scale corresponds to ±50 mm at that stated percentage. Choose the range and any higher-precision option around the tolerance your task needs. The published ±0.2% FS/year stability describes change over time; temperature, liquid conditions and installation are reviewed separately when defining the complete measurement requirement.

faqs.question: What information helps match the sensor to our liquid?
paragraphs: Share the liquid composition and concentration, operating temperature, density behavior, suspended solids and cleaning conditions. These details allow the probe, seals and cable to be reviewed against the actual process. Water, effluent, oils and chemical solutions can need different configurations. Include the vessel pressure and required accuracy in the same brief so Hitelecom can define a suitable sensing arrangement and confirm compatibility for the supplied parts.

faqs.question: How can the probe cable and mounting be adapted to our site?
paragraphs: The published product supports customization of range, probe cable length and mounting. Specify the probe position, tank or well depth and route to the communication terminal, including service access and protection from mechanical loads. The terminal's mounting lugs, pole clamp or slotted mount depend on configuration. Agree how the submerged probe is positioned and supported separately, then document its level reference and cable route for commissioning.

faqs.question: How can we obtain stable readings in wastewater or a busy sump?
paragraphs: Choose a sensing position that represents the collection level and remains accessible for inspection. Review inlet turbulence, sediment accumulation, scaling and the liquid's chemical conditions with the probe selection. Suitable support or a protective arrangement can help maintain a consistent position, while an inspection plan keeps the sensing surface and cable in useful condition. Share the sump layout and expected solids so these details can be included in the installation proposal.

faqs.question: How do tank pressure conditions affect the measurement setup?
paragraphs: Tell Hitelecom whether the vessel is open, vented or pressurized. The H Series is published as a submersible level sensor; confirm the selected probe's measurement principle and pressure reference during configuration. For a pressure-based arrangement, an open or vented tank needs an appropriate atmospheric reference, while a sealed vessel requires the liquid-surface pressure to be considered. Review these details alongside the liquid density and level range.

faqs.question: Can level readings help estimate the volume stored in a tank?
paragraphs: Yes, when the tank geometry or a validated level-to-volume table is available. Level is a height reference; converting it to stored volume depends on the vessel shape and the chosen datum. Share the tank dimensions or calibration table, along with the required display units, so the calculation and receiving-platform implementation can be agreed. For irregular or horizontal tanks, use the appropriate conversion across the working level range.

faqs.question: Which wireless option fits our factory or remote water site?
paragraphs: Choose the connection around reception at the terminal, regional network support, reporting needs and the receiving platform. The published family lists 4G LTE, NB-IoT and LoRa options. For cellular projects, review the available operator coverage and selected modem configuration. For LoRa, include the gateway and server path in selection. Check the complete route from the installed terminal to the dashboard before completing site commissioning.

faqs.question: How can we connect level data to our own platform?
paragraphs: The published 4G and NB-IoT deployment sends level readings through MQTT to Hitelecom Cloud or a customer platform. Share the receiving endpoint, authentication approach, payload requirements and device identifiers so the integration can be agreed. Hitelecom Cloud also provides dashboards and configurable alarm rules. For a LoRa deployment or a project involving controllers, confirm the gateway, server and interface path as part of the supplied solution.

faqs.question: How should we balance reporting frequency and battery life?
paragraphs: Set the profile around how quickly the level changes and when the team needs to see it. The published battery reference is more than 10 years at four-hour reporting under specified test conditions. Actual runtime depends on the model, sensing and sampling demand, reporting frequency, temperature, signal coverage and retransmissions. Agree the required measurement and notification timing, then request a battery-life estimate for that configuration and site profile.

faqs.question: How can high and low alerts support refill and drainage operations?
paragraphs: Set high and low thresholds around the site's usable reserve, refill plan or collection capacity. Define the person who reviews each notification and the follow-up action, then verify the complete alert path during commissioning. For automated pump or valve operation, include the controller or PLC, suitable interfaces and operating logic in the project. The required response timing is agreed for the complete system, from level measurement through the selected control equipment.

faqs.question: What should we include in an application-specific quotation request?
paragraphs: Send the application, liquid specification, maximum level, vessel pressure and required tolerance, along with a site photo or drawing. Add the probe position, cable route, process and ambient temperatures, fouling conditions and inspection access. Include the wireless region, reporting profile, platform and any controller integration. Where the project needs contact approvals or hazardous-area documentation, identify the exact requirement so the proposed configuration and supporting evidence can be reviewed together.

applicationSection.title: Liquid level monitoring applications.
applicationSection.description: Explore eight application groups across factory water storage, cooling utilities, process water, effluent recovery, drainage, industry-specific water systems, dewatering and source water. Each context identifies the level trend, sensing point and project details that help select a useful configuration.
applicationSection.note: Illustrative application images. Configure each monitoring point for the actual liquid and installation.

applications.title: Factory raw-water buffer tanks
applications.description: Maintain a clear view of stored raw water before it feeds treatment and production. A level trend helps the utilities team compare incoming supply with plant demand, plan replenishment and investigate an unexpected drawdown. Configure the monitored span around the usable storage depth and agree the low-level notification point with the operating team.
applications.measurement: Liquid height and replenishment / drawdown trends in the raw-water buffer.
applications.monitoringPoint: A representative compartment of the supply tank, referenced to the agreed tank datum.
applications.installation: Choose an accessible probe position away from the inlet jet and withdrawal suction. Route the cable to an above-liquid terminal with usable radio coverage.
applications.projectBrief: Tank depth, inlet / outlet arrangement, normal working levels, raw-water composition and required notification timing.

applications.title: Process-water day tanks
applications.description: Keep day-tank replenishment aligned with production shifts. A local liquid-level reading gives operators a shared reference for water available to the next process, while historical readings help explain repeated refill cycles. Specify the working band, reserve level and reporting needs for the actual day tank rather than selecting the maximum family span by default.
applications.measurement: Water level within the day tank’s operating band, plus refill and consumption patterns.
applications.monitoringPoint: The day tank supplying the selected production line or process-water distribution point.
applications.installation: Provide an approved probe suspension or guide and service access. Locate the sensing point clear of filling splash and protect the cable along the full route.
applications.projectBrief: Usable depth, water temperature, refill cycle, required low-level response and connection to the chosen platform.

applications.title: Treated service-water storage
applications.description: Monitor treated water after the plant’s treatment stage and before it is distributed to users. Comparing levels over time helps the utilities team understand storage recovery and demand during busy periods. Pair the readings with treatment and transfer-pump operating records when reviewing performance, and select probe and cable materials for the actual treated-water chemistry.
applications.measurement: Stored treated-water level and recovery after transfer or production demand.
applications.monitoringPoint: The service-water holding tank downstream of the specified treatment stage.
applications.installation: Use a stable, accessible immersion point with an agreed zero reference. Confirm water chemistry, temperature and cleaning practice before specifying the wetted assembly.
applications.projectBrief: Treatment type, tank dimensions, working levels, water composition, cable route and reporting requirements.

applications.title: Gravity-fed service-water tanks
applications.description: Follow the available head in a vented gravity-fed service tank. The water level can help operators plan a refill and understand a decline in supply to the served area. Connect the measurement to the tank’s own reference elevation and operating band, so readings from different tanks remain meaningful to the team reviewing them.
applications.measurement: Liquid level in the gravity tank and the available operating band above the outlet.
applications.monitoringPoint: The vented service tank feeding the relevant building or industrial service area.
applications.installation: Confirm tank access, cable support and the approved terminal location. Account for the probe position and tank datum when commissioning the displayed level.
applications.projectBrief: Tank elevation, outlet level, refill arrangement, liquid suitability and the required reserve notification.

applications.title: Emergency water-reserve monitoring
applications.description: Maintain visibility of a water reserve that may be checked less frequently than production storage. Level trends support routine inspections, replenishment planning and investigation of an unexplained fall. Include the reading in the site’s reserve-management procedure, with the required alert recipients and response time agreed by those responsible for the installation.
applications.measurement: Reserve-water level and changes between planned inspections.
applications.monitoringPoint: The designated reserve tank or compartment, using its documented operating levels.
applications.installation: Select a serviceable immersion point and protect the cable and terminal from mechanical damage. Specify any approval or independent protection requirements in the project brief.
applications.projectBrief: Reserve purpose, usable depth, permitted installation work, required approvals and notification / inspection workflow.

applications.title: Cooling-tower basin levels
applications.description: Track the water held in a cooling-tower basin through changes in load, evaporation and make-up supply. A level history helps the maintenance team review recurring replenishment issues and schedule inspections. Select the sensing point and wetted assembly around circulating-water treatment, basin turbulence and the practical access available during normal maintenance.
applications.measurement: Cooling-basin water height and refill / drawdown patterns.
applications.monitoringPoint: A representative basin compartment away from the strongest return flow and pump intake.
applications.installation: Use the approved probe guide or support to maintain a repeatable position. Assess treatment chemicals, temperature, debris and cleaning access for the supplied assembly.
applications.projectBrief: Basin depth, circulating-water chemistry, working temperature, maintenance access and required reporting profile.

Monitoring this storage point helps the utilities team review replenishment demand and arrange attention before the selected reserve level is reached. Define the tank being measured and its pressure conditions clearly, particularly where it sits beside a separate pressurized cooling circuit.
applications.measurement: Liquid level and replenishment frequency in the make-up storage tank.
applications.monitoringPoint: The identified vented make-up or buffer tank, with its own level datum.
applications.installation: Confirm the tank pressure condition, liquid treatment and accessible probe position. Keep the cable clear of pumps and equipment-service routes.
applications.projectBrief: Tank type, usable depth, water treatment, room layout, pressure condition and expected replenishment cycle.

applications.measurement: Supply-water level and replenishment trends during evaporative-cooling operation.
applications.monitoringPoint: The dedicated water supply or circulation tank serving the selected cooling unit.
applications.installation: Choose a quiet, accessible immersion point clear of the return jet. Confirm water treatment, liquid temperature and cable protection for the equipment layout.
applications.projectBrief: Cooling arrangement, tank dimensions, operating seasons, water chemistry and required notification recipients.

applications.monitoringPoint: An accessible storage stage before the boiler-feed or steam equipment, as specified by the plant.
applications.installation: Confirm the selected liquid temperature and vessel pressure against the supplied configuration. Plan access and cable routing independently of hot equipment and steam lines.
applications.projectBrief: Storage-stage drawing, normal / maximum temperature, pressure condition, water treatment and required level span.

applications.monitoringPoint: The dedicated utility-water tank feeding the selected humidification system.
applications.installation: Confirm the wetted assembly, cleaning method and expected water temperature. Position the terminal where maintenance access and radio coverage are both practical.

applications.title: Metal-component rinse tanks

A level trend supports refill planning and helps operators review changing use across shifts. Identify the exact rinse chemistry and temperature, including contamination carried in from the previous process, then select the probe and cable around that defined liquid.

applications.monitoringPoint: A defined rinse tank or its water-supply buffer, separated from other process baths.
applications.installation: Plan probe placement around part handling and tank cleaning. Confirm compatibility with the actual rinse liquid and maintain service access without obstructing production.

A time-stamped level record helps maintenance and production teams compare refill events with operating cycles and investigate unusual consumption. Specify the rinse stage separately from detergents or other baths, and include the cleaning and service conditions in the proposed sensor configuration.

applications.monitoringPoint: The rinse reservoir or clean-water buffer serving the selected parts washer.

applications.title: Treated-effluent holding tanks
applications.description: Observe treated effluent held before reuse, transfer or discharge under the site’s operating procedure. Time-stamped levels help staff review storage recovery and plan attention to the selected operating band. Include the remaining liquid constituents, expected deposits and service access in the configuration so the measurement point suits this final holding stage.
applications.measurement: Treated-liquid level and changes between storage, transfer or reuse events.
applications.monitoringPoint: The final holding tank or a defined treated-effluent storage compartment.
applications.installation: Select a stable immersion point clear of inlet and outlet disturbances. Confirm liquid suitability and make the cable route and probe retrieval accessible for routine service.
applications.projectBrief: Treatment stage, liquid composition, tank dimensions, discharge / reuse workflow and required reporting intervals.

applications.title: Sludge-supernatant collection
applications.description: Track the separated liquid collected from a sludge-handling process. This monitoring task focuses on the supernatant-water level in its receiving tank, giving operators a reference for return or transfer planning. Identify residual solids and the collection arrangement so the probe position and inspection routine are selected around the liquid being measured.
applications.measurement: Separated-liquid level in the supernatant collection tank.
applications.monitoringPoint: The identified liquid receiving compartment downstream of sludge separation.
applications.installation: Assess residual solids and fouling before choosing the assembly. Keep the probe above accumulated deposits with approved support and practical access for inspection.
applications.projectBrief: Separation process, residual-solids conditions, receiving-tank depth, return cycle, cleaning access and liquid temperature.

applications.title: Healthcare wastewater collection
applications.description: Monitor wastewater collected before a healthcare facility’s specified treatment stage. Level history can help facilities staff plan inspections and review collection versus transfer through the day. Confirm the exact wastewater composition, disinfection and cleaning practices with the site team, then select a configuration and installation procedure appropriate to that collection point.
applications.measurement: Collected-wastewater level and transfer trends in the nominated receiving tank.
applications.monitoringPoint: The designated wastewater holding or collection stage in the facility’s treatment system.
applications.installation: Plan protected cable routing and retrieval using the facility’s approved access procedure. Confirm liquid and cleaning compatibility along with any required installation approvals.
applications.projectBrief: Wastewater composition, disinfectants, temperature, tank depth, site-access conditions and notification workflow.

applications.title: Plant-room drainage sumps
applications.description: Record rising and falling water levels in plant-room sumps that collect seepage, condensate drains or utility leakage. A documented sensing point helps the maintenance team compare normal collection with unusual accumulation and plan an inspection before the pit reaches its operating limit. Review the inflow pattern, drainage arrangement and alert timing together, then select the probe position and reporting profile around the actual sump.
applications.measurement: Collection level and drawdown relative to the sump's operating marks.
applications.monitoringPoint: An accessible, representative part of the pit away from the main inlet and pump intake.
applications.installation: Provide stable probe support, cable protection and inspection access. Mount the wireless terminal above the expected water level and verify reception in the plant room.
applications.projectBrief: Sump section, liquid sources, operating levels, pump arrangement, temperature, inspection access, coverage and required alert timing.

applications.title: Factory washdown collection
applications.description: Observe collection levels as factory washdown water passes from floor drains into a holding pit or tank. Comparing the level trend with cleaning schedules helps the team review collection capacity and the timing of removal or transfer. Specify the detergents, process residues and solids present so probe and cable selection fits the liquid. Define practical alert levels around the tank's working volume and operating routine.
applications.measurement: Level buildup during washdown and reduction after transfer or removal.
applications.monitoringPoint: A representative collection compartment downstream of the drain entry, with a defined level reference.
applications.installation: Route the cable clear of cleaning equipment and provide access for residue inspection. Review the probe position, protection and wireless terminal location with the cleaning layout.
applications.projectBrief: Cleaning schedule, detergent and residue details, solids, collection depth, transfer arrangement, temperature and notification workflow.

applications.title: Factory stormwater lift stations
applications.description: Track water collection and drawdown at a factory stormwater lift station during rainfall and the period afterward. The level record gives site operators context for drainage inspections, pump-operation review and unusual accumulation. Match the reporting profile to the expected speed of change, then agree thresholds and recipients with the drainage team. Include sediment, debris, seasonal water levels and the separate pump-control arrangement in the project brief.
applications.measurement: Wet-well level during storm inflow and subsequent drainage.
applications.monitoringPoint: The wet well at a stable position outside the strongest inlet jet and pump suction zone.
applications.installation: Plan probe support and access for debris inspection. Keep the terminal accessible above the expected water line and confirm coverage at the lift station.
applications.projectBrief: Catchment and wet-well layout, level marks, inflow changes, debris, pump controller, coverage, reporting and response requirements.

applications.title: Underground lift-pit monitoring
applications.description: Follow water accumulation in an underground lift pit serving industrial parking, service access or below-grade utility areas. A consistent level reference helps maintenance staff compare routine seepage with a changing drainage pattern between visits. Plan alerts around the pit's usable depth and the team's inspection workflow. Review access, sediment, cable routing and radio reception before selecting the installation, with pump automation defined through the site's controller.
applications.measurement: Standing-water level and the trend between drainage cycles.
applications.monitoringPoint: The accessible collection pit at a position clear of moving equipment and strong suction.
applications.installation: Protect probe and cable from service work and document the reference depth. Evaluate an accessible terminal position with a verified wireless path from the below-grade site.
applications.projectBrief: Pit drawing, maximum level, seepage sources, service access, pump system, terminal location and notification timing.

applications.title: Industrial containment collection

Review accumulation against inspection and removal records to support the site's handling plan. Share the liquid composition, cleaning method and possible changes in content so a matching probe and cable can be evaluated. Select the range and alert profile around the collection arrangement.
applications.measurement: Collected-liquid level relative to the tank's defined handling and inspection marks.
applications.monitoringPoint: A designated collection compartment with known liquid conditions and access for assessment.
applications.installation: Agree the wetted configuration, stable probe support and cable route for the specified contents. Include site classification and service access in the installation review.
applications.projectBrief: Collected liquid and concentration, potential variation, tank depth, temperature, pressure, cleaning, site requirements and handling workflow.

Define the utility function and the water's contact designation in the project brief so the required documentation and wetted configuration can be reviewed. applications.measurement: Service-water storage level through utility demand and replenishment cycles.
applications.monitoringPoint: A clearly identified utility-water tank with documented function, level marks and liquid conditions.
applications.installation: Plan probe positioning and cable routing around tank access and cleaning. Mount the communication terminal for inspection and confirm the water-contact requirements for the actual application.
applications.projectBrief: Utility purpose, water specification and contact requirements, storage depth, temperature, cleaning method, network and reporting profile.

applications.monitoringPoint: A service-water storage point whose use and operating conditions are defined by the facility.
applications.installation: Coordinate probe and terminal placement with utility access and tank cleaning. Specify any contact, documentation or site requirements with the exact supplied configuration.

applications.title: Paper-mill water-recovery tanks

applications.monitoringPoint: An agreed water compartment, with fiber and sediment conditions documented for probe selection.
applications.installation: Provide access for sensing-surface inspection and route cables clear of transfer equipment. Review turbulence, fouling and probe support around the chosen compartment.
applications.projectBrief: Recovery stream, fiber and solids content, chemistry, temperature, tank geometry, transfers, cleaning and required monitoring timing.

applications.projectBrief: Recycling-stage layout, alkalinity, solids and settling pattern, maximum level, cleaning, equipment movements, platform and reporting.
